entities.name: Giovanni Domenico de Cupis
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Giovanni Domenico de Cupis (1493–1553) was an Italian Cardinal, created by Pope Leo X in the consistory of 1 July 1517.

Born in Florence, Italy, de Cupis was a member of the powerful Medici family and was appointed as the Archbishop of Siena in 1522.

De Cupis played a significant role in the Italian Reformation, particularly in the city of Siena, where he worked to promote the teachings of the Protestant reformer, Martin Luther.

He was a key figure in the creation of the Accademia dei Fusi, a prominent literary and artistic academy in Siena.

De Cupis died on December 20, 1553, at the age of 60.

His legacy as a cardinal and a reformer has endured, and he remains an important figure in the history of the Italian Reformation.

In the words of one of his contemporaries, 'De Cupis was a man of great piety and learning, who dedicated his life to the service of God and the promotion of the Gospel.'
